# Ads Performance & Auction Health Analytics

SQL, Python and Excel analysis of a food-delivery marketplace's ad business: KPI reporting, inventory and auction health, category and retention insights, opportunity sizing, and an A/B test readout.

**All data is synthetic.** It is a simulated 1% sample of ad logs (Jan-Sep 2026, INR), generated by `generate_data.py` with a fixed seed. The simulator sets the mechanics (auction pricing over a floor price, capacity limits, advertiser churn, and a known treatment effect in the A/B test), so the value of this project is the analysis, not the numbers.

## Run it
```bash
pip install numpy pandas openpyxl
python generate_data.py      # builds ads.db (SQLite, ~2.4M impressions, ~1 min)
python run_analysis.py       # runs queries.sql -> results/*.csv + A/B statistics
python build_workbook.py     # builds Ads_Analytics_Workbook.xlsx
```

## Schema
`advertisers` (category, signup_date, budget) · `slots` (floor CPM) · `inventory` (daily available vs filled) · `impressions` (timestamp, advertiser, slot, cpm_paid, num_bidders, variant) · `clicks` · `orders` (attributed order value)

## Contents
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `queries.sql` | Weekly KPIs, category performance, auction health, cohort retention, top advertisers per category (window functions), WoW growth, A/B readout, ROAS fix list, revenue concentration |
| `Ads_Analytics_Workbook.xlsx` | KPI dashboard, category view, retention, auction health, opportunity-sizing model, A/B readout, metric definitions (all formula-driven) |
| `results/` | CSV output of every query |

## Findings (on the simulated data)
1. Fill rate rose from 39% to 91% as advertisers ramped. `search_top` and `restaurant_listing` are ~100% sold out in recent weeks; `home_banner` is ~69% filled with 32% single-bidder auctions, so its lever is demand, not price.
2. ROAS ranges from 4.6x (QSR Chains) to 0.78x (Personal Care). Snacks & FMCG is 24% of spend at 1.46x.
3. Local Restaurants return ~4.0x ROAS but only 19% are still spending at day 90 (n=16), a retention problem. Cohorts are small, so treat as directional.
4. Top 10 advertisers account for ~40% of spend.
5. Opportunity sizing (scenario model; inputs are assumptions): base case adds ~3.3% to ad revenue across a premium search placement and home_banner sell-through.
6. A/B test (dish-image carousel format): CTR +25.4% (95% CI +14.9% to +35.9%, p < 0.001), CPM unchanged. The click-to-order guardrail has only ~9% of the clicks needed to detect a 15% drop, so the recommendation is a monitored rollout or a holdout.

## Limitations
Synthetic data, small retention cohorts (n = 5-16), scenario inputs in the sizing model are judgement calls, and the A/B treatment effect is set in the simulator.
